correctness.rationale: For every strict coordinate order the exposed coordinate selection yields either the two-coordinate outer vertex or the single-exception three-coordinate inner vertex; conversely every listed vertex is exposed. Regularity makes all outer coordinates have the same squared norm, with inner deficit exactly 2(r-1). The outer-vertex barycenter certifies the exact unique circumball. Nonnegative coordinates bound every pair distance by twice the common outer squared norm, with equality exactly for disjoint outer supports. A closed matching count in the q-regular complement certifies existence and number of all equality pairs. Strict convexity excludes nonvertex contacts and diameter endpoints. Schrijver 1978 supplies the chromatic-number theorem for the cycle corollary. Exact independent finite exposed-vertex enumeration checked 16 small admissible graphs; general proof does not infer universality from tests.

originality.rationale: Full-text primary comparison: 2026 cyclic interval hypergraphic-poset paper treats lattice and poset properties, and 2006 general simplex Minkowski-sum study treats faces and vertex combinatorics, rather than these metric equality classifications. Schrijver 1978 proves only the graph colouring ingredient, not the Euclidean realization. Published geometric results on graphical zonotopes, symmetric-edge polytopes, and star hypergraphic polytopes have distinct summands, geometries, or graph parameters. Targeted semantic-record and web searches plus all accessible own earlier claim summaries did not find a covering statement. Historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: A separately indexed geometry paper or unpublished result may already contain this exact regular-graph hypergraphic Euclidean metric theorem.
The Schrijver chromatic conclusion is not new as an abstract graph theorem: only the exact Euclidean diameter-graph realization and associated metric classification are claimed.
Nonregular graphs and other affine embeddings are not covered; finite exact tests are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The exact metric, circumradius, all contact vertices, diameter graph, and matching count simultaneously classify a natural infinite, graph-indexed polytope family. The striking universality of metric scalars under regularity contrasts with the graph-specific geometry of the edge-disjointness diameter graph. The cyclic subfamily gives a concrete Euclidean diameter-graph realization of the unbounded-chromatic Schrijver family. None follows merely from the initial hypergraphic-poset lattice structure.
